focus.jnote: The surface is calm but the floor is not. After Friday’s weak September payrolls — just 29K jobs, unemployment ticking to 4.2% — an October Fed hike came off the table, stocks closed near record highs and the VIX fell to ~15.3. But three live wires remain: the US–Israel war on Iran drags on with the Strait of Hormuz contested and a third US carrier group heading to the region; the 10Y sits near ~5.26%, just off its highest since 2002; and oil is near $90 (Brent above $102) even after the G7 agreed to release 100M barrels of emergency reserves. Gold is holding ~$4,150. Futures are a touch lower ahead of ISM Services at 10:00 ET. This is a headline-and-rate tape, not one a Sniper sells premium into — and the scanner confirmed it: zero names cleared the criteria today.
focus.notdown: Energy (XLE, XOM, CVX, OXY) keeps a war-premium bid with Brent above $102 and Hormuz still contested — but oil actually slipped today on the G7 reserve release, showing this is a two-sided supply-shock trade, not a clean Sniper. One de-escalation or export-normalization headline and crude gives back the premium. Watch-only. Semis / high-beta growth led Friday on the no-hike relief, but that’s momentum, not a durable catalyst. Nothing here cleared validation.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive groups (REITs, utilities, housing, small caps) stay pressured with the 10Y near ~5.26% and oil feeding inflation fear. But selling bear calls into a VIX this low, with a live war that can squeeze shorts on any de-escalation headline, carries its own violent-reversal risk — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~52 is in WARM and P(≥1% gap) at 36% is just above the 35% trigger — either one alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: an active military conflict with an oil market running at $90+ is an unscheduled, open-ended tail, stacked on a bond market at ~5.26% multi-decade-high yields. The full-universe scanner ran successfully and boarded ZERO names. A low VIX is not a green light when the gap tail is headline-driven and skewed. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the headline window and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

risks: US–Israel war on Iran & the Strait of Hormuz — Iran has ruled out reopening the strait, a third US carrier group is heading to the region, and Houthis claimed an attack on a Riyadh Aramco facility. Any strike on Gulf oil infrastructure or personnel gaps the whole tape instantly. This is the number-one thing to watch.

Bond yields — 10Y near ~5.26%, just off 2002 highs — the 10Y touched above 5.34% recently before easing on the soft jobs print. A firm ISM or a hot inflation read could send yields back up and hit rate-sensitive growth, REITs, utilities and small caps hardest.

Oil near $90 / Brent above $102 — even after the G7 agreed to release 100M barrels of reserves and OPEC+ held November output steady, core-member output runs ~5M bpd below prewar levels. Any fresh disruption sends crude vertical and feeds inflation fear.
ISM Services · today 10:00 ET — consensus ~55.7 vs 55.4 prior. A still-hot services read while inflation has only just softened would revive yield pressure; a soft read supports the Fed-hold story.

Low VIX complacency & Q3 earnings ahead — a VIX near ~15 understates headline tail risk from an open-ended war, and Q3 earnings season (big banks ~mid-Oct) plus the Nov 3 midterms are building single-stock and event risk just as the macro tape stays on edge.
